name: Umar Nakamura

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group. We have no ties to employers, AI firms, unions or government. Your answers stay confidential. What does a normal workday look like for you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I lead a crew fitting exterior cladding and windows on building sites. My vocational trade certificate was a start; what I pass to apprentices now is how to spot water running behind a frame before it stains the wall. I earn well for this work and like being trusted with the awkward openings. My wife Layla and I have two school-age children, a mortgage and about eleven months of expenses saved, with plenty of other contractors nearby. I have never used AI and I take my measurements with a tape and level.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the crew the office may have a quicker form, but the window still has to keep rain out. A measured window sill matters more than a tidy screen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My pay and hours should stay as they are, and our savings cover a short gap if a site pauses. I would not buy a new tool for paperwork that barely changes the fitting job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep my current window and cladding shifts and check the sill fall with a level. In the first year I would return any new form missing the measured opening before ordering a frame.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm. The children still need breakfast and the mortgage still gets paid from my work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What makes a sill fail?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A sill set almost level lets rain sit against the frame instead of running away. I would show the apprentice the small fall with the level before the seal goes on.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you try AI if the office offered it?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, not for saving a few minutes. I have not used it before and would rather keep the measurements I already trust.

say: **Measured sills** keep rain out of fitted windows even when an office form is quicker.
**Faster forms** do not replace a level.
think: My **pay and hours** stay secure in the plateau.
Our **eleven-month reserve** can cover a short site pause.
do: **Keep** current window and cladding shifts while measuring sill fall with a level.
**Return** new order forms missing measured openings.
S0.quote: A measured window sill matters more than a tidy screen.
fieldNote: He has **never used AI** and teaches apprentices to judge water flow by a real level.
High **trade pay and savings** make the mild scenario financially secure.

steps.text: Keep window and cladding shifts with measured sill checks

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say booking and buying can move onto software before a robot fits a window on a wall. I want job times checked on old openings before anyone shortens the schedule.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A standard frame can arrive for an opening that leans, leaving us to remake it under pressure. I expect my own wage to hold because the crew has work and nearby contractors want fitters, but the rush could make apprentices miss a leak.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would record six window jobs with measuring, rework and sealing time, then show the figures to the site manager. In the first year I would keep my crew’s normal checks and accept shorter targets only after a field trial fits safely.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about being hurried, secure about our income. A leaking new window can do more damage than a late finish.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which opening would test a new schedule?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The old brick opening on our current site narrows by the top course. I would write the two widths on the order and record the time to fit the frame.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you join a protest about targets?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. I would first take the measurements to the person setting the schedule and ask for a proper trial.

say: **Booking and buying** change before capable robots can fit windows on building sites.
**Old openings** need field times before shorter schedules.
think: A **rushed frame** could cause a hidden leak.
My **own pay** looks secure given current work and nearby firms.
do: **Record** six window jobs with measuring and sealing times.
**Accept** shorter targets only after safe field fitting trials.
feel: **Uneasy** about rushed apprentices, secure about wages.
S1.quote: A leaking new window can do more damage than a late finish.
fieldNote: His **schedule concern** is about leaks, with little immediate risk to his own pay.
He chooses a **measured trial** with the manager before any wider campaign.

steps.text: Keep normal window checks while six jobs are timed
Wait for safe fitting trial before accepting shorter targets

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the crew thinking AI can change buying and drawings by 2028, while fully capable fitting robots arrive about 2031. We still have three years of hands-on windows and cladding in the gap.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could lose part of my high-paid fitting work after 2031 if a machine handles old openings well. We have eleven months saved and many local firms, yet the same pay will not be guaranteed at another site.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would compare our regular bills with my base wage, then ask nearby contractors about posted senior fitting openings. If robots cut shifts after 2031, I would apply for a posted local role only if its wage covers our bills and its safety duties are clear; I would not spend the household reserve on a course without a real post and paid time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about losing a good wage, but not stranded. I have room to compare actual work instead of taking the first promise.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What safety duty would you ask about?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Who checks a robot-fitted window for water running behind the frame after a storm? I would want a named worker with authority to reject a leaky fitting.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could you retire instead?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, I am forty-three and the children are still in school. Our eleven months of savings are a buffer, not a replacement for years of window-fitting wages.

say: **2028 thinking AI** changes drawings before capable robots can fit windows and cladding around 2031.
think: Robots could cut **high-paid fitting shifts** after 2031.
Eleven months saved and **local firms** help, but equal wages are uncertain.
do: **Compare** base fitting wage with regular bills.
**Apply** after 2031 for posted local senior fitting only if bill-covering pay and clear safety duties.
feel: **Anxious** about replacing a strong wage, with options nearby.
S2.quote: Our eleven months of savings are a buffer, not a replacement for years of window-fitting wages.
fieldNote: He rejects **early exit** at forty-three and treats savings as search time.
His **application** needs shift cuts, a posted local role, bill-covering pay and clear safety duties.

steps.text: Apply after 2031 for posted local bill-covering fitting if shifts fall and duties safe

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years would let a contractor test a fitting robot through several rainy seasons before thinking AI reaches the office in 2031. Capable field machines arrive around 2034, and I would want a worker to sign off the weather seal.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The children will be older and we may owe less on the mortgage, but I cannot assume that now. I could learn inspection work if the trade proves useful and a contractor pays for practice; I would not leave a well-paid crew for a training leaflet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep leading window jobs and watch a real robot fitting on an old opening. If a posted local weather-seal inspection role offers a place on paid hands-on training, safe sign-off authority and wages that cover our bills, I would complete the course before 2031 and apply in the first year after 2031.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about losing fitting shifts, but five years gives me a chance to see a leak test. I would trust a wet wall and a dry room more than a robot sales film.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the leak test show?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The crew would spray the outside and check the inside edge for water after the robot seals it. I would want failed joints counted, not repainted and called finished.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If the pay is lower than fitting windows?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Layla and I would compare the posted wage with mortgage, food and school costs. I could take a drop if it covered those bills, but not if we had to use savings every month.

say: **Rainy-season trials** should precede capable robots fitting windows on buildings around 2034.
**Human sign-off** should cover window weather seals.
think: A **seal inspection** post could suit me after a real leak trial.
The **mortgage and children** need bill-covering wages.
do: **Watch** an old-opening robot fitting and leak test.
**Complete** paid hands-on seal training for posted local safe bill-covering role.
**Apply** after 2031 if trained and written safety authority remains.
feel: **Anxious** about losing high-paid shifts despite time to see a real leak test.
S3.quote: I would trust a wet wall and a dry room more than a robot sales film.
fieldNote: His **resistance** softens after a real site leak test, not a screen demonstration.
His **training and application** require paid time, a course place, posted local vacancy, safe authority and bill-covering wage.

steps.text: Observe robot fitting and leak test on old window opening
Complete paid seal course for posted local safe bill-covering role if place offered
Apply after 2031 for posted local bill-covering seal job with rejection authority if trained

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A decade means thinking AI by 2036 and capable building robots around 2039. I would use those years to pay more off the mortgage. A window is only good if it keeps the weather outside after the fitting robot leaves.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will be in my fifties when the field robots arrive, with working years left. Savings and plenty of local firms give us room, but a machine that fits safely could still lower what I earn at the end of my career.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the crew job and put an extra eighty from each pay cheque toward the mortgage if ordinary bills allow. In the first year after 2036 I would apply for a posted local weather-seal inspection job only if an employer-paid training place is offered, the safety sign-off is real and its wage covers household bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about later wages, though I have time to bring the mortgage down. I would rather rely on a paid job than a promise about machines.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would the extra payment work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Layla and I would send eighty beyond the normal mortgage payment after each full pay cheque. We would pause it if school bills rose, rather than take from the eleven-month reserve.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you teach the children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show them a window sill that drains and one that holds rain, then let them touch the difference. They can choose any trade, but I want them to understand workmanship.

say: **2036 thinking AI** precedes capable robots fitting windows on buildings around 2039.
**Weatherproof work** remains a useful lesson for children.
think: Later **high-paid shifts** might shrink after robots spread.
Savings and **local firms** give time to reduce mortgage debt.
do: **Pay** eighty extra toward mortgage from each cheque if bills allow.
**Apply** after 2036 for posted local seal inspection only with paid training, safe authority and bill-covering wage.
feel: **Anxious** about later pay, with time to lower debt.
S4.quote: A window is only good if it keeps the weather outside after the fitting robot leaves.
fieldNote: His **extra debt payment** comes from new wages, apart from the reserve already held.
His **later application** keeps training, safe authority, posted local work and bill-covering pay conditional.

steps.text: Keep leading window and cladding work
Pay eighty extra on mortgage from full cheques if bills allow
Apply after 2036 for posted local bill-covering seal role with offered paid course and safe authority

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most, because a capable fitting robot around 2031 could take well-paid window jobs before the children finish school. A posted local weather-seal job with paid hands-on training, safe sign-off and bill-covering pay would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who pays when a robot seals a window badly. I want the person who signs a robot-sealed window job to be able to reject a leak before the wall is closed.

portrait: **Umar Nakamura**, 43, leads window and cladding work with a vocational trade certificate.
He and wife Layla have **two school-age children**, a mortgage, higher pay and about eleven months of expenses saved.
He has **never used AI** and trusts a level, wet-wall tests and paid work over new software.
In **AGI by 2031**, he considers paid weather-seal inspection only after a real course place and safe sign-off duties.
The **2028 picture** worries him because robots could reduce well-paid fitting shifts while family costs continue.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could cut higher-paid window-fitting shifts around 2031 while mortgage and school costs continue.
whatWouldHelp: A posted local **seal inspection role** with paid training, safe authority and bill-covering pay would protect income.
headlineQuote: I want the person who signs a robot-sealed window job to be able to reject a leak before the wall is closed.
